name: redirect-uri-input
title: Redirect URI Input
description: Checks a redirect URI the way an OAuth server does (exact string match), highlighting a differing trailing slash, scheme, case, www or port against the registered list with a one-tap swap, plus localhost in production, wildcards, fragments and stray whitespace.

meta.summary: Catches OAuth redirect URIs that are close to but not exactly the registered one, plus unsafe ones like localhost in production or wildcards.
meta.server: The authorization server must compare redirect_uri by exact string match against the registered list.
catches: Near-misses against registered URIs: trailing slash, http vs https, case, www, port
Side-by-side highlight of the differing characters, with a one-tap swap
localhost or loopback in a production client
Wildcards, a #fragment, default :443 port, empty ? and stray whitespace
Short custom schemes for native apps
limits: Checks the string only; it cannot see what your provider actually has registered unless you pass it
Providers differ (some allow loopback port variation for native apps); follow your provider's rules
Not a substitute for server-side exact matching
a11y: Visible <label> tied to the input; aria-invalid on errors
Status summary in a polite live region linked by aria-describedby
After a one-tap fix, focus returns to the input
Match state shown with icon and text

sources.label: RFC 9700 – OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice

rules.note: Confirmed: RFC 9700 requires exact string matching of redirect URIs, except variable port numbers for localhost redirect URIs of native apps.
